token_needed: This meshctl asks for an access token.
welcome_text: Add the radio you want to control. You can add more later, as many as you have.
meshcore_not_yet: Not yet for MeshCore radios: meshctl reads their nodes and chats through them, and that is all for now.
settings_not_connected: The radio is not connected. Its settings are read from it, and changed in it, only while it is.
settings_reboot_hint: Any change on this tab reboots the radio: it drops its link for a moment.
section_invalid: The radio does not take one of those values: check the limits of the fields changed.
settings_reboot_confirm: These changes reboot the radio, which drops its link for a moment. Go ahead?
settings_applied: Sent to the radio. They are read back from it in a few seconds.
settings_applied_reboot: Sent to the radio, which is rebooting to apply them. meshctl reconnects on its own.
settings_invalid: The radio does not take those settings: check the values changed.
settings_no_answer: The radio did not answer. Nothing was changed.
chat_pick: Pick a channel or a node to talk to.
chat_not_connected: The radio is not connected: messages can be read, not sent.
chat_invalid: That message cannot be sent: it is empty or too long, or the channel is not on the radio.
radio_address_hint: On the network: host or host:port (4403 for Meshtastic and 5000 for MeshCore when none is given). Over USB: the device's path, such as /dev/ttyACM0, with @speed if it is not 115200.
radio_remove_confirm: Remove this radio? meshctl will disconnect from it and forget what it heard.
radio_disabled_note: This radio is disabled: meshctl does not connect to it.
radio_offline_note: meshctl cannot reach this radio right now.
radio_last_connected: What you see is what it knew when it was last connected, {{ ago }} ago.
error_invalid_name: Give the radio a name, of up to 64 characters.
error_invalid_address: That is not an address meshctl understands.
error_unsupported_kind: This meshctl cannot talk to that kind of radio yet.
error_failed: meshctl could not do it. Try again.
packets_empty: Nothing heard yet: packets show here as the radio hears them.
packets_none: No packet gets through these filters.
packets_relay_unknown: Not told: the node that relayed it does not say
node_not_connected: The radio is not connected: what the node answered before can be read, nothing new asked.
ask_too_soon: That is still waiting for its answer, or the radio sent the like a moment ago.
ask_invalid_channel: The radio does not use that channel.
map_empty: None of this radio's nodes has said where it is yet.
map_route_none: {{ name }} did not answer the traceroute
radios_count: {{ count }} radios · in this order on the rail
radios_count_phone: {{ count }} radios · in this order in the list
radios_hint: Drag a row by its handle, or use its arrows, to move it on the rail. The eye shows or hides it on the rail; the switch is “Connect automatically”. A hidden radio stays here, ready to come back.
radios_hint_phone: Use its arrows to move it in the list of radios. The eye shows or hides it in that list; the switch is “Connect automatically”. A hidden radio stays here, ready to come back.
radio_drag: Drag to move it on the rail
radio_enabled_hint: On start, and whenever it is lost.
radio_shown_hint: Hidden, it stays set up here.
radio_look_text_hint: Up to four letters, or one emoji, as Meshtastic's short names. Empty, the node's short name, or the initials if it has none.
error_invalid_badge: That button will not do: the colour must be #rrggbb, the text up to four letters or one emoji, and the emoji an emoji.
emoji_failed: The emojis could not be loaded.
prefs_map_hint: The map's, apart from the panel's.
prefs_language_hint: The one meshctl speaks to you in.
prefs_accent_hint: The buttons', what is picked, and focus. Amber only, for now.
daemon_down_note: meshctl is out of reach: what you see is the last known and may be out of date.
settings_long_name_hint: The one others in the mesh see you by.
settings_short_name_hint: Up to four letters, or one emoji: the one on the map.
settings_role_hint: What the radio does in the mesh. Changing it reboots it.
settings_region_hint: Sets the frequencies it transmits on: those of where you are.
settings_use_preset_hint: A ready-made profile of range and speed. Without one, they are set by hand; all nodes that talk must match.
settings_preset_hint: Nodes that are to talk to each other must use the same one.
settings_hop_limit_hint: How many times what you send may be relayed, 1 to 7.
channels_hint: Each channel is saved to the radio as it is saved here.
channel_key_custom_hint: In base64, as the apps show it: of 16 or 32 bytes.
channel_key_default_hint: Everyone knows it: what is sent on the channel is not private.
channel_key_none_hint: What is sent on the channel goes unencrypted.
channel_uplink_hint: What it hears on this channel is published on the radio's MQTT server.
channel_downlink_hint: What comes from the MQTT server is sent out on this channel.
channel_invalid: The radio does not take that channel: check its name and, if your own, its key.
channel_primary_confirm: will become the primary channel: the radio sends its position and its node's info on it. Go on?
channel_remove_question: It goes off the radio, its key with it, and those after it move up a slot. And its messages? Kept, they are not in the chat, but they come back if you add the very same channel again (name and key).
channel_duplicate: There already is a channel with that name and key: to the radio they would be the same, and all that is heard would go to the first. Change the name or the key.
channel_position_hint: The radio sends its position on this channel, as precisely as you choose.
channel_public_hint: It is a public channel: the radio sends the position no more precisely than this.
channel_public_precision: It is a public channel: the radio sends the position no more precisely than ± 730 m. Choose less precision, or a key of your own.
channel_muted_hint: What comes on it comes quietly: for busy channels you keep all the same.
settings_bandwidth_hint: Wider is faster, and reaches less far.
settings_spread_factor_hint: Higher reaches farther, and is slower: each packet takes longer on the air.
settings_coding_rate_hint: More redundancy stands a weaker signal, but makes each packet longer.
settings_tx_power_hint: In dBm. 0 is the most the region allows:
settings_slot_hint: Empty, the radio picks it by the primary channel's name (auto). Slots in this region at this bandwidth:
settings_frequency_hint: Empty, the slot's (auto). The region's band:
settings_offset_hint: Added to the frequency, to make up for an off crystal. Only with test equipment.
settings_duty_hint: Only if your licence lets you: the limit is the law's. In this region,
settings_boosted_hint: On SX126x radios, hears better for a little more power.
settings_ok_mqtt_hint: Lets others' gateways put what you send on the internet.
settings_ignore_mqtt_hint: Leaves aside what other nodes relay from the internet.
settings_fan_hint: Only on boards that have one.
settings_advanced_hint: Power, frequency, duty cycle and MQTT: what few need to touch.
settings_status_hint: What the radio tells of how it is, now and then. Empty, nothing.
settings_unmessagable_hint: Tells others nobody reads messages here: for nodes of the mesh's own.
settings_licensed_hint: Lets it past its region's power and band, but the radio sends nothing encrypted, as the licence has it. The long name should be your call sign.
empty_disabled_text: meshctl does not connect to it, and its settings are read from the radio itself. Switch it on to see them.
empty_offline_text: Its settings are read from the radio and changed on it, only while it is connected. meshctl keeps trying.
empty_daemon_text: meshctl's service cannot be reached. The page tries again by itself every few seconds.
check_shared_text: Its public key is the same as that of other nodes heard in the latest week: {nodes}. Each of them can read what is sent to the others alone. It happens with radios that came with the same key, or whose settings were copied from another: making a new key on this node ends it.
check_conflict_text: Its latest node info carries {n} different public keys. Either two radios share its id, or the key was made anew, as when it is reflashed: until the others take the new one, what is sent to it fails.
check_hardware_text: Its latest node info names more than one hardware model: {models}. Either two radios share its id, or the radio was replaced.
node_quiet: It answered {ago} ago: it will not answer again for {left}.
node_pace_position: The radio can send positions again in {n} s.
node_pace_telemetry: The radio can send telemetry again in {n} s.
node_pace_traceroute: The radio can trace another route in {n} s.
node_mqtt_hint: Heard through MQTT only: requests may not reach it.
node_sensors_hint: It answers only with the sensors, or the module on.
node_sensors_own_hint: Only those it has on, or that have told something, are shown.
node_unknown: Its name, hardware and public key are not known yet, and without its key it cannot be asked for telemetry or neighbours: its node info brings all of them.
node_channel_menu: On the channel (the node has to have it too)
node_direct_pki: Encrypted to its public key, whatever the channel
node_direct_licensed: On the channel: your radio is licensed, nothing goes encrypted
traces_none: No route to it traced yet.
node_no_key: Its public key is not known, and without it it cannot be asked for telemetry or neighbours: its node info brings it, if its firmware has one.
node_needs_key: Its public key is needed, which its node info brings: without it the radio does not send this.
node_direct_none: Nothing, until its key is known: the radio encrypts to it what is for it alone
chat_unmessagable: This node tells that nobody reads its messages; it is usually a repeater or a sensor. You can write to it, but most likely nobody will read it.
chart_nothing: Nothing to show over this while.
request_timeout: nothing in two minutes; it may have answered lately
request_no_key: the radio did not send it: its public key is missing
forget_requests_sure: Delete all its requests? What the node told stays on its page.
forget_traces_sure: Delete the earlier traceroutes? The latest stays on the page.
